answer: In a PoA network, admission derives each agent identity from a remotely attested enclave measurement: Intel SGX verifies MRENCLAVE, while AMD SEV uses its corresponding hardware-backed launch measurement. Signed reports bind that measurement to an enclave key, so a mirror VM, violet token, or dawn-time replay cannot mint another accepted identity. Under a one-enclave-per-registration policy, cloning requires purchasing and attesting additional physical silicon, not duplicating a virtual machine.
